historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle judgment: ~1% long-run US housing-starts growth + ~2.5% product price inflation; neither the 3-yr (peak-to-trough) nor the 5-yr (BMC merger Jan-2021 doubled the base) CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every 3-yr CAGR is measured FY2022 peak -> FY2025 and every 5-yr CAGR spans the Jan-2021 BMC merger (FY2020 revenue $8.6B -> FY2021 $19.9B); equity 5-yr (+30%) diverges from revenue 5-yr (+12%) by more than 30% and from the 3-yr series by sign. None is a growth signal. Owner-FCF CAGRs (FY2025 $770M, FY2022 $3,193M, FY2020 $131M) track reported FCF closely because SBC is only ~0.5% of revenue; SBC is not where the cash went.
historical_growth.notes: Cyclical: FY2022 is the peak, FY2026E the trough. Forward growth is the recovery path to a mid-cycle anchor, not a CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Housing stays flat through 2027 as affordability binds, then single-family starts recover from ~880-925k toward a ~1.03M mid-cycle level over FY2028-30. Revenue compounds +2/+6/+7/+6% to ~$17.7B by FY2030 (no M&A revenue projected; acquisition spend is outside the flows), and pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs from the ~7.5% trough to 11.5% - the midpoint of FY2025 (9.4%) and FY2024 (13.5%) and close to the FY2023-26E ex-boom average of 11.4%. Value-added mix (48% of sales) and the $60-70M cost-outs offset QXO-era price pressure. Cash tax ramps 21% -> 24%; working capital absorbs 10c per dollar of growth. Terminal 2.5% growth with a 14x owner-FCF cap; the count is held flat and buybacks fund it.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage rates ease in 2027, the structural underbuild asserts itself and single-family starts run toward 1.15M by 2029-30. Revenue grows +5/+10/+10/+7% to ~$19.6B by FY2030 while operating leverage, value-added mix and productivity restore an FY2024-type 13.5% pre-SBC margin. BLDR consolidates share from under-capitalized independents through the recovery, QXO stays disciplined on price, and buybacks continue at $0.3-0.5B/yr. Terminal 3.0% with a 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The downturn broadens: FY2027 revenue falls another 4% as single-family starts slip to ~850k and multi-family keeps contracting; margins compress to 6.5% on deleverage and lumber deflation. The recovery from FY2028 is shallow (+3-4%) and QXO's Beacon/GMS roll-up turns commodity lumber and specialty categories into a price war, so the mid-cycle pre-SBC margin settles at 9.0% - pre-merger distributor economics rather than the post-merger 'structurally higher' claim. Net debt/EBITDA stays near 4x for several years, limiting buybacks and M&A; no covenant or refinancing event (nearest notes 2030, $1.5B liquidity), so no solvency floor is hit. Terminal 2.0% with a 12x cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Through-cycle owner-FCF DCF on a housing cyclical at the trough of a four-year downturn. The valuation does not extrapolate the FY2022 peak (lumber boom, 18.9% margin) or the FY2026E trough (7.5%); it discounts a recovery to a stated mid-cycle revenue and margin anchor and capitalises the mature year at a cyclical-appropriate 12-15x owner FCF. Leverage (~4x) and cycle risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a stacked WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin anchor: every 1pp of terminal pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly $10/share; the 11.5% base is a judgment between FY2025 (9.4%) and FY2024 (13.5%).
Timing of the housing recovery: the base assumes starts turn in FY2028; each year of delay removes a year of recovering FCF and keeps leverage near 4x.
QXO (Beacon, GMS) could compress industry pricing or bid up tuck-in multiples; BLDR's M&A-driven growth is outside the flows, so acquisitions that are value-destructive would not show here.
Leverage amplifies equity value: net debt is ~68% of the current market cap, so a 10% move in enterprise value is a ~17% move in equity value.

D&A above capex (acquired-intangible amortisation) adds a modest tax shield in the early years; BMC intangibles are largely non-deductible, so the engine's shield is slightly generous (~0.1-0.2% of revenue).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 49.67-131.50
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via BLDR_Metrics.csv (FY2008-Q3 2026); FY2025 10-K (BLDR_Annual_FY2025.txt) and Q3-2026 10-Q (BLDR_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for the balance sheet, diluted shares, SBC, equity-award taxes, leases and debt composition; FY2026 guidance from the Q3-2026 earnings release as summarised in BLDR_Analysis.json
data_sources.qualitative: BLDR_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): bull/bear axes, QXO competitive dynamics, housing-starts forecasts, guidance history

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = midpoint of the FY2026 net-sales guidance of $14.2-14.6B narrowed at Q3-2026 (9M-2026 actual $11,003.7M + a seasonally weak Q4 of ~$3.4B). TTM to 30-Sep-2026 is $14,361.6M. FY2025 actual was $15,190.6M.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q3-2026 (10-Q EPS note, 107,635k). 1,134k antidilutive/contingent RSUs excluded by the filer; not added because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Count held FLAT; buybacks of $303.5M in 9M-2026 (3.3M shares) under the $500M April-2026 authorization are funding the flat count.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30-Sep-2026: SBC add-back $43.2M (FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement $53,512k + 9M-2026 10-Q $36,484k - 9M-2025 $46,800k) plus cash taxes on equity awards $16.1M (financing activities: FY2025 $29,323k + 9M-2026 $13,946k - 9M-2025 $27,191k). The filer publishes no combined figure in the 10-K/10-Q, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 full-year combined was $82.8M (0.55% of revenue).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print)
inputs.net_debt_note: Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet: long-term debt net of current maturities $4,615.1M plus current maturities ~$4.1M = $4,619.2M total debt (includes ~$0.2B of finance lease and other finance obligations per the FY2025 10-K); cash $55.0M. Net debt $4,564.2M against FY2026E company-adjusted EBITDA of $1.075-1.125B is ~4.1x. Liquidity ~$1.5B (undrawn $2.2B revolver less letters of credit) so no refinancing event inside the horizon; nearest senior notes mature 2030.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.5 for a levered housing cyclical -> cost of equity ~11.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.2% (6.375% 2032/2034 and 6.75% 2035 notes), ~4.7% after 24% tax. Market weights: equity $6.7B (107.6M x $62.54) / debt $4.6B = 59/41 -> WACC 8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. Held identical across all three scenarios: cyclicality and leverage are charged in the scenario flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations file, item f).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating-lease rent (~$150M/yr; operating lease liabilities $661.3M at 30-Sep-2026) is already inside EBITDA and OCF, so no lease line is deducted and operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial (<$2M) but, with ~$0.2B of other finance obligations, sit inside total_debt per the filer's own debt note; their interest is in financing cost, which is outside the unlevered flows. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. No non-controlling interests; net income is 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, through-cycle framing per SKILL.md row 'operating company, cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations.md. BLDR is the largest US structural building-products distributor/manufacturer; value is a stream of operating FCF, so the owner-FCF engine applies. WHY THROUGH-CYCLE: FY2022 (pandemic housing boom + lumber at $1,000+/mbf) was a 6x peak on net income ($2.75B) and FY2026E is the trough of a 4-year housing downturn (net sales $14.4B, adjusted EBITDA margin ~7.6%, TTM owner FCF $192M). Neither year is a base. Pre-SBC EBITDA margins (GAAP EBITDA + SBC) on the post-BMC footprint: FY2021 14.9%, FY2022 18.9%, FY2023 16.3%, FY2024 13.5%, FY2025 9.4%, FY2026E ~7.3% (guided company-adjusted 7.4-7.9% includes other add-backs). Excluding the two commodity-boom years the FY2023-26E average is ~11.4%; pre-merger BLDR and BMC ran 7-8%. Base mid-cycle anchor: 11.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin reached FY2030 on ~17.7B revenue (FY2026E +23%: single-family starts 880-925k back to ~1.03M mid-cycle, ~2.5%/yr product inflation, modest share gain from value-added mix; no M&A revenue is projected because acquisition spend is not deducted from the flows). Bull 13.5% on ~19.6B (FY2024-type margin at 1.15M single-family starts); bear 9.0% on a 2027 leg down and a slow recovery with QXO-driven price competition. TERMINAL: Gordon vs cap, cap set at 14x (base), 15x (bull), 12x (bear) owner FCF - the 12-15x range the method prescribes for cyclicals; the cap is expected to bind in base and bull. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor (receivables + inventory > payables, net ~$1.64B = 11% of TTM revenue), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE: growth consumes ~10c per $ of revenue growth. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax rate ~13% (bonus depreciation under the 2025 Act), FY2026 distorted by the $43.9M IRS R&D settlement; ramped 21% -> 24% (21% federal + state). D&A 3.9% of revenue in FY2025 includes ~$250M/yr acquired-intangible amortization (largely non-deductible BMC merger intangibles); path declines to 3.0% as those roll off, against capex held at 2.4% (guided 2-2.5%). SBC is 0.4-0.55% of revenue (held 0.5%), so the house/street band is narrow. Street basis: SBC as non-cash. Interest income: none material (net debt company), 0. SANITY: base year-1 (FY2027) owner FCF ~$0.5B on a 7.5% margin vs TTM $192M at ~7.3%; the difference is the tax and working-capital swing, not a margin leap. Base mid-cycle owner FCF ~$1.1-1.2B/yr (FY2030) vs FY2023/FY2024 reported FCF of $1.83B/$1.49B at higher margins.

bear.narrative: A further leg down in FY2027 (single-family starts ~850k, multi-family still falling, Texas/Colorado weak), then a slow recovery capped by QXO-driven price competition; mid-cycle margin reverts toward pre-merger distributor economics at 9.0%.

base.narrative: FY2027 flat-to-slightly-up (industry composite: 2026 starts flat, affordability still binding), recovery FY2028-30 as single-family starts normalize toward ~1.03M; revenue reaches ~$17.7B and pre-SBC EBITDA margin 11.5% by FY2030, between FY2025 (9.4%) and FY2024 (13.5%). No M&A revenue.

bull.narrative: Mortgage-rate relief in 2027 starts a multi-year single-family recovery toward 1.15M starts; value-added mix and cost-outs restore an FY2024-type 13.5% pre-SBC margin on ~$19.6B by FY2030.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because net debt/adjusted EBITDA is ~4.1x at the trough, FY2026 guidance was cut twice intra-year (no visibility into the bottom), and a well-funded consolidator (QXO) is a new structural competitor; the bear case is a margin and duration problem, not solvency ($1.5B liquidity, no maturities before 2030), so it is not raised further. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things - rate relief, a starts recovery to 1.15M, and QXO price discipline - to all go right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
